en: The amihan brings cool, dry northeast winds to the Philippines between November and February, causing lower humidity and less rainfall across the archipelago.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is a perfect cone stratovolcano that frequently erupts, producing fast-moving clouds of hot gas and rock called pyroclastic flows.
Romblon province contains high-quality marble deposits, which are metamorphic rocks formed from original limestone under intense subterranean heat and immense pressure.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a direct underground flow from a mountain cave to the sea, demonstrating groundwater discharge.
The nutrient-rich volcanic soil surrounding Mount Mayon in Albay provides essential minerals like potassium and phosphorus for growing healthy local abaca plants.
The three bright stars forming the Balatik constellation, part of Orion in Western astronomy, are actually massive, hot blue supergiants located far beyond our solar system.
The Philippine Trench is a deep oceanic subduction zone where tectonic plates collide, causing the powerful earthquakes that frequently strike eastern Mindanao.
Tropical cyclones entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility gain destructive energy from the warm Pacific Ocean waters, which evaporate to provide massive amounts of atmospheric moisture.
During a full moon, the aligned gravitational pull of the moon and sun creates high spring tides that flood coastal areas in Manila Bay.
Miners in Masbate extract metallic gold from hydrothermal veins, demonstrating how hot, mineral-rich water deposits valuable elements into rock fractures deep underground.
The Bataan peninsula experiences a dry climate because the Zambales Mountains block moisture-laden clouds, creating a distinct rain shadow effect over the area.
The Diwata-2 microsatellite travels through low Earth orbit, using optical sensors to capture images of clouds, oceans, and landmasses for national weather forecasting.
